_doc: Determinism-harness fixture: 20 queries + 20 passages spanning 5 clear-cut topical clusters (4 each). Each query's expected top-1 passage is in the same cluster. Inter-cluster cosine distance is large; intra-cluster top-k ordering is the gate.

passages.text: Jupiter has four large moons known as the Galilean satellites: Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.
Saturn's rings are composed mostly of water ice with traces of rocky material and dust.
Mars has two small, irregularly shaped moons named Phobos and Deimos.
Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system and the closest to the Sun.
A supernova is the explosive death of a massive star at the end of its life cycle.
The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy containing roughly 100 to 400 billion stars.
A black hole forms when the core of a very massive star collapses under its own gravity.
Red dwarfs are the most common type of star in the Milky Way galaxy.
Quicksort is a divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm with average O(n log n) time complexity.
A hash table stores key-value pairs and offers average O(1) lookup time.
Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve smaller subproblems.
A binary search tree maintains sorted data and allows O(log n) average lookup.
The French Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of the Bastille on July 14.
World War II ended in 1945 following the surrender of Japan in September.
The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, marking a major moment in the Cold War's end.
The Western Roman Empire fell in 476 AD when the last emperor was deposed.
The mitochondria are organelles that generate most of a cell's supply of ATP energy.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert sunlight into chemical energy.
Human DNA is organized into 23 pairs of chromosomes in each somatic cell.
The heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles.
